grammar.title: Pertanyaan tidak langsung
grammar.explanation: Setelah pembuka sopan seperti 'Could you tell me', 'Do you know', atau 'I wonder', susunan kalimatnya kembali seperti kalimat biasa (subjek dulu, baru kata kerja). Untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak, pakai 'if' atau 'whether'.
examples: Could you tell me where the registration desk is?
Do you know what time the keynote starts?
I wonder if the talks are recorded.

common_mistake.wrong: Could you tell me where is the registration desk?
common_mistake.right: Could you tell me where the registration desk is?

grammar.title: Used to untuk kebiasaan masa lalu
grammar.explanation: Pakai 'used to + V1' untuk kebiasaan atau keadaan di masa lalu yang sekarang sudah tidak berlaku. Bentuk negatif dan tanya memakai 'did' dan 'use to' (tanpa -d).
examples: I used to work in an office.
Did you use to travel for work?
I didn't use to drink coffee.

common_mistake.wrong: I use to travel a lot when I was younger.
common_mistake.right: I used to travel a lot when I was younger.

reading.title: How to beat jet lag
reading.text: Jet lag happens when your body clock is out of sync with the time zone you are in. Flying east is usually harder than flying west, because it is more difficult to go to bed earlier than to stay up later. Experts suggest a few simple steps. Before you travel, start moving your bedtime one hour closer to the new time zone. On the plane, drink plenty of water and avoid too much coffee. When you arrive, get as much daylight as you can, since light is the strongest signal for your body clock. Short naps are fine, but try not to sleep for more than twenty minutes. Most people adjust at a rate of about one day per time zone, so a trip from Jakarta to London may take almost a week to recover from fully.

options: Going to bed earlier is more difficult

writing.prompt: Kamu baru pulang dari konferensi teknologi. Tulis email ke timmu: ceritakan dua hal yang kamu pelajari, satu orang menarik yang kamu temui, dan satu ide yang ingin kamu coba bersama tim.
checklist: Dua hal yang dipelajari dengan penghubung (First, Also)
Past simple untuk kejadian di konferensi
Satu usulan dengan 'I'd like to try ...' atau 'What if we ...?'
useful_phrases: I wanted to share a few highlights.
I ran into ..., who used to ...
One idea I'd like to try is ...
writing.model_answer:
Hi everyone,

I'm back from the tech summit, and I wanted to share a few highlights.

First, the keynote on speech recognition showed how small teams can add voice search with free browser tools. Also, a design workshop reminded me that we should test our screens with real users more often, not just with our own team.

I also ran into Hana, a developer who used to work on voice apps in Melbourne. She offered to share her testing checklist, and we agreed to keep in touch.

One idea I'd like to try is a short user test every Friday: fifteen minutes, three users, one feature. It wouldn't take much time, and we'd catch problems earlier.

What do you think? I'm happy to explain more at Monday's stand-up.

Best,
Bagus

speaking.prompt: Gaya IELTS Speaking Part 1: ceritakan perjalanan paling berkesan yang pernah kamu lakukan. Ke mana, dengan siapa, dan apa yang paling kamu ingat? (4 sampai 5 kalimat)
speaking.sample_answer: The most memorable trip I've taken was to Yogyakarta with my university friends. We used to travel together every year, but we hadn't done it for a while. We spent most of the time getting around the city by motorbike and trying street food. What I remember most is watching the sunrise at Borobudur, even though we had to wake up at three. I'd love to go back with my family one day.
